question: Your agent helps engineers understand a legacy codebase. It must call the MCP tool index_legacy_modules before it uses Grep or Read. An engineer set tool_choice to {"type": "tool", "name": "index_legacy_modules"} on every request in the agentic loop. The index is now always built first, but the agent calls index_legacy_modules again on every turn and never reaches Grep or Read. Which two statements about this design are accurate?

options.text: The loop stalls because the forced setting stays on later requests, while the following steps should be processed in follow-up turns without that forcing.
options.reason: The pattern forces only the first call and then processes the later steps in follow-up turns. Keeping the forced setting makes the model call the same tool on every turn.

options.text: The loop stalls because the MCP server returns its index results without the isError flag, so the agent treats each call as unfinished and retries it.
options.reason: The isError flag marks a failed tool call. A successful result without it does not cause repeats. The forced tool_choice on each request makes the model call the tool again.

options.text: Forced tool selection works only for built-in tools such as Grep and Read, so the MCP tool must be made first through its tool description instead.
options.reason: Forced selection names any tool, such as the custom extract_metadata tool in the guide's example. It already works here, because the index is always built first.

options.text: Forcing index_legacy_modules on the first request is the right mechanism, because it guarantees that this tool is called before any other tool.
options.reason: Forced tool selection makes the model call the named tool, so it ensures that a specific tool is called first. This is the first part of the pattern.

options.text: The loop stalls because the agent has too many tools, so removing Grep and Glob from allowedTools would let it move past the indexing step.
options.reason: Too many tools degrades tool selection, but here the forced tool_choice decides the tool. Fewer tools would not stop the forced call on each request.
